abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal cancers in the western world and is largely resistant to treatment. A major barrier to effective treatment is the highly desmoplastic and immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment, where the organisation of tumour, stromal and resident immune cells limit immune infiltration. B7-H3 (CD276) is an emerging immune checkpoint marker investigated in phase I and Ib/2 clinical trials in PDAC, yet its biological role within the tumour environment remains poorly understood. We performed an integrated multiscale spatial profiling study to map B7-H3 expression across regional and single-cell spatial contexts in treatment-naive resected human PDAC. Furthermore, we explored the B7-H3 landscape in the neoadjuvant setting. Our results demonstrate that B7-H3 is not simply overexpressed in cancer but may act as a spatial organiser of the PDAC microenvironment, associated with a transition from epithelial-intrinsic tumour architecture to fibro-inflammatory immune states that underpin immune suppression, aggressive disease and poor prognosis. This fibro-inflammatory state appears conserved within the neoadjuvant landscape.

title: B7-H3 Orchestrates Fibro-Immune Spatial Organisation in Pancreatic Cancer
